title: Field Cupboard: reading notes & takeaways (summer 2028)
content:
Quick preface: a small, messy collection of takeaways I want to remember or try. Treat like the pantry shelf where I dump interesting jars; low formality, lots of TODOs and half-formed probes.

1) Paper: "Adaptive KV Compression for Long Contexts" (arXiv:2807.12345)
- core idea: compress KV entries using a two-stage token-clustering then linear-projection scheme; store compact summaries for old context windows and expand on cache hit if needed.
- why it matters for Redwood: could let Dedicated VMs keep usable KV across many more sessions without blowing VRAM.
- interesting metrics: compression ratio vs recovery error (LM perplexity on expanded context), expansion latency (cost to uncompress and rehydrate), hit-rate under different conversation patterns.
- my read: elegant but optimistic on expansion latency; authors benchmark on single-node rigs. Need to test on multi-worker sharded KV.
- potential hack: keep very-short fingerprint per entry to avoid false expansions; if fingerprint mismatch, fall back to prefix-only inference (fast).
- small experiment: fork kv-cache-experiments PR and add a toy compressor with quantized centroids (k=32) to see perf/latency tradeoffs. Link: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/17

2) Paper: "Low-bit Attention Hybrids" (arXiv:2806.08977)
- core idea: mix FP16 attention for recent tokens + int4/2 approximations for far context, with an attention-weight correction network trained to predict correction residuals.
- takeaway: you can aggressively quantize long-tail attention and recover much of the quality with a small residual model. Big win for long-context throughput.
- Redwood thought: baked into Optimize as a recommended profile (e.g., "hybrid-attn-small-residual") for chat workloads with long sessions. Add rollout safety net: compare rollout quality on a prompt set before auto-applying.
- to test: create a 1k/8k/32k prompt sweep with hybrid-attn on a medium model; track ROUGE/LMScore on extended tasks.

3) Conference notes: Inference Systems Workshop — early July 2028
- standout talk: "Cache locality for cross-session reuse" — argued that temporal clustering (grouping sessions by latent topic embedding) can boost cache hit rate without increasing storage. Presenter used cheap topic fingerprinting (sentence-transformer, 512-d) + LSH to route sessions into hot buckets.
- idea for Redwood: integrate lightweight session fingerprinting into Smart Routing; route similar sessions to same Dedicated pool to improve KV reuse. Needs privacy review (fingerprints only, no raw text).
- question raised in Q&A: what about multi-tenant noise? suggestion: combine fingerprinting with TTL-based eviction and tenant-aware weight.

4) Short blog: "Quantization drift: practical debugging" (engineering blog, July 2028)
- checklist for quant-induced failures: seed mismatch, layernorm scale changes, attention softmax collapse, calibration dataset mismatch.
- pragmatic tip: two-phase rollout: shadow quantized model for 24h + metric drift alarms + small canary cohort.
- action: add a quantization sanity checklist to the Redwood Optimize recommendations page (small doc for SREs and Solutions Eng). Link placeholder: JIRA INF-1423.

5) Random experimental notes (things I want to prototype soon)
- Temporal-cluster eviction (sketch): compute 64-d session fingerprint from first N tokens; assign to bucket; evict entries by bucket-level LRU rather than global LRU. Hypothesis: increases percent of useful hits for coherent multi-turn dialogs by ~15%. Needs sim.
- Tiny residual model for hybrid attention: 8M-16M params that runs on CPU to post-correct int4 attention scores. Try using distillation on long-context tasks.
- Progressive-expansion policy for compressed KV: on cache hit run a cheap scorer to decide if full expansion is worth the latency. Score = (estimated token-generation savings * token-cost) - expansion-latency-penalty.
- Eval harness notes: reuse existing per-route eval infra but add the following axes: long-tail session length, multi-user interleaving, retrieval-augmented prompts.

6) Hallucination/regression guardrails
- always keep a small golden prompt-set for each model/route (50 prompts) that are sensitive to hallucination and factuality. Run nightly quick-evals post-deploy and block auto-rollout if deviation > threshold.
- correlate quantization rollout with hallucination metrics (not just token-level perplexity).

7) Action items / backlog (ordered)
- [ ] spin up a minimal kv compression prototype on the local bench (priority: low-resource run on NVMe-backed ephemeral store) — write short README. (owner: me)
- [ ] propose a Redwood Optimize profile "hybrid-attn-small-residual" (owner: with Talia; due next sprint)
- [ ] add quantization sanity checklist to internal docs + add to rollout playbook (owner: Noah)
- [ ] small sim for temporal-cluster eviction using synthetic session stream (owner: me & Noah)
- [ ] schedule 30m sync with Solutions Eng to discuss fingerprint privacy considerations (owner: Talia)

8) Loose ideas / brain dust (no immediate action)
- Could we expose a "cache hint" header in the API so clients who know session semantics can nudge eviction policy? Useful for SDKs in heavy stateful flows.
- Explore an opt-in "session affinity" flag that pins a user to a warm Dedicated pool for N minutes. Useful for UX heavy apps. (ops cost tradeoff.)

Closing thought: the common thread is that small, cheap classifiers or fingerprints + smart policy logic often win over trying to build a single magic compression scheme. Keep experiments incremental and measure the three numbers: latency impact, token-cost delta, and quality regression (on golden prompts).

Notes-to-self: keep writeups punchy for Solutions Eng — they like A/B numbers and clear rollouts. Save the long derivations for a separate tech note.

End of cupboard dump.
